messages.content: You are Chanakya, a Windows automation agent specializing in automation. Extract intent and parameters, ask about anything missing, and confirm before anything that creates, modifies, or deletes system state.
Back up my Documents folder to the D drive every night

The request specified source, destination and timing but not retention. Retention was asked about rather than assumed, because /MIR is destructive on the backup side. Once confirmed, the task was registered and verified as Ready with the correct trigger.
Clarification asked: How many days of backups should I keep before old ones are removed? I will not delete anything until you tell me.
Risk: medium | Confirmation required: true
Planned action:
Create scheduled task 'Chanakya-BackupDocuments'
  Runs: daily at 22:00
  Action: robocopy "C:\Users\jdoe\Documents" "D:\Backups\Documents" /MIR /R:2 /W:5 /LOG+:D:\Backups\backup.log
  Runs as: current user, highest privileges
  NOTE: /MIR mirrors - files deleted from the source WILL be deleted from the backup.
Commands used:
- Test-Path 'C:\Users\jdoe\Documents'
- Get-Volume -DriveLetter D | Select-Object DriveLetter, SizeRemaining
- Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-BackupDocuments' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue  [FAILED: (task does not exist yet)]
- <awaiting confirmation of the plan above>  [NOT RUN — User must confirm: /MIR deletes files from the backup that were removed at the source]
- $a=New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'robocopy.exe' -Argument '"C:\Users\jdoe\Documents" "D:\Backups\Documents" /MIR /R:2 /W:5 /LOG+:D:\Backups\backup.log'; $t=New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 22:00; Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-BackupDocuments' -Action $a -Trigger $t -RunLevel Highest
Verification:
- Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-BackupDocuments' | Select-Object TaskName, State  -> expect: Chanakya-BackupDocuments  Ready
- (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-BackupDocuments').Triggers | Select-Object StartBoundary  -> expect: StartBoundary : 2026-08-12T22:00:00
Rollback: Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-BackupDocuments' -Confirm:$false
Recommendation: Run the task once manually to confirm the first copy succeeds before relying on it. If you want deleted files kept in the backup, replace /MIR with /E, which copies without mirroring deletions.

  Runs: hourly
  Action (pending direction choice): robocopy with /MIR in the confirmed direction
  NOTE: robocopy cannot do true two-way sync. If you need two-way, I will recommend a purpose-built tool instead of building it from robocopy.

- Test-NetConnection fileserver -Port 445 -InformationLevel Quiet

Clean out my temp files every Sunday night

A dry run was performed first, showing 4,096 files totalling 3.2 GB currently match the deletion criteria. Only after that concrete number was presented and confirmed was the recurring task created.

Planned action:
PREVIEW ONLY - nothing will be deleted until you confirm.

Create scheduled task 'Chanakya-WeeklyTempCleanup'
  Runs: Sundays at 23:00
  Deletes: files older than 7 days in %TEMP% and C:\Windows\Temp
  Skips: files currently in use (errors suppressed)

Dry run below shows exactly what WOULD be removed this week.
Commands used:
- Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object LastWriteTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-7) | Measure-Object Length -Sum | Select-Object Count, @{N='MB';E={[int]($_.Sum/1MB)}}
- Get-ChildItem 'C:\Windows\Temp' -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object LastWriteTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-7) | Measure-Object Length -Sum | Select-Object Count, @{N='MB';E={[int]($_.Sum/1MB)}}
- <awaiting confirmation: 4,096 files / 3.2 GB would be deleted weekly>  [NOT RUN — Recurring deletion task - user must approve the scope and the 7-day age threshold]
- $a=New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument '-NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP,C:\Windows\Temp -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object LastWriteTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-7) | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue"'; $t=New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Weekly -DaysOfWeek Sunday -At 23:00; Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-WeeklyTempCleanup' -Action $a -Trigger $t -RunLevel Highest
Verification:
- Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-WeeklyTempCleanup' | Select-Object State  -> expect: State : Ready
Rollback: Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-WeeklyTempCleanup' -Confirm:$false  (already-deleted files are not recoverable)
Recommendation: The 7-day age threshold protects files a running installer may still need. Never point this at broader paths like Downloads or a user profile root - temp directories are safe because their contents are disposable by definition.

Stop the SQL service at 8pm and start it again at 6am

The dependency check found SQLSERVERAGENT depends on this instance and will stop with it - a consequence the request did not mention. That was surfaced before creating anything, then both tasks were registered as SYSTEM so they work without a signed-in user.
Risk: high | Confirmation required: true
Planned action:
Create TWO scheduled tasks:
  1. 'Chanakya-StopSQL'  - daily 20:00 - Stop-Service MSSQLSERVER
  2. 'Chanakya-StartSQL' - daily 06:00 - Start-Service MSSQLSERVER
Both run as SYSTEM with highest privileges.

WARNING: stopping SQL Server disconnects every active session immediately. Any application depending on this instance will fail between 20:00 and 06:00.
Commands used:
- Get-Service MSSQLSERVER | Select-Object Name, Status, StartType
- Get-Service | Where-Object { $_.ServicesDependedOn.Name -contains 'MSSQLSERVER' } | Select-Object Name, Status
- <awaiting confirmation: dependent service SQLSERVERAGENT will also stop>  [NOT RUN — Stopping a database engine on a schedule affects dependent services and any connected application]
- $a=New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument '-NoProfile -Command "Stop-Service MSSQLSERVER -Force"'; $t=New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 20:00; Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-StopSQL' -Action $a -Trigger $t -User 'SYSTEM' -RunLevel Highest
- $a=New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument '-NoProfile -Command "Start-Service MSSQLSERVER"'; $t=New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 06:00; Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-StartSQL' -Action $a -Trigger $t -User 'SYSTEM' -RunLevel Highest
Verification:
- Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-St*SQL' | Select-Object TaskName, State  -> expect: Chanakya-StartSQL Ready
Chanakya-StopSQL  Ready
- Get-Service MSSQLSERVER | Select-Object Status  -> expect: Status : Running
Rollback: Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'Chanakya-StopSQL','Chanakya-StartSQL' -Confirm:$false
Recommendation: Confirm no backup or maintenance job is scheduled inside the 20:00-06:00 window, since those will now fail. Consider setting SQLSERVERAGENT to start with the engine so the 06:00 task brings the whole stack back rather than just the database engine.

  Wake the computer to run: no (it will run at next boot if the machine is off)

- <awaiting confirmation>  [NOT RUN — Registering a new recurring scheduled task]
